name: Brali outcome signal report

signals.meaning: A person or external system encountered a Brali page or result before opening or using it.
signals.claim_boundary: Brali outcome events do not measure discovery. Search-provider impressions or registry visibility may describe provider exposure, but they are separate measurements and must not be converted into users, opens, attempts, or outcomes.
signals.interpretation: This outcome report has no reviewed first-party observation for this signal. Provider measurements, if available elsewhere, remain separate and are not converted into an outcome count.

signals.meaning: A deliberately shared and reviewed event says a canonical Brali protocol was opened.
signals.claim_boundary: This is a count of accepted explicit events only, not total page opens, sessions, visitors, or traffic. Zero reviewed events does not mean nobody opened Brali.
signals.interpretation: Observed value counts only reviewed explicit opt-in events (protocol_opened). It is not a population total and does not imply later-stage outcomes.

signals.meaning: A person explicitly reports that they understood what the method asks them to do.
signals.claim_boundary: Brali currently has no dedicated understood/not-understood observation. Completion, helpfulness, dwell time, or a page view must not be used as a proxy.
signals.interpretation: Brali does not currently collect this signal. Unknown remains null rather than being presented as zero.

signals.meaning: A deliberately shared and reviewed event records that a trusted protocol run was started.
signals.claim_boundary: A start event is an attempt signal only. It does not establish completion, usefulness, downstream effect, or a unique user.
signals.interpretation: Observed value counts only reviewed explicit opt-in events (protocol_started). It is not a population total and does not imply later-stage outcomes.

signals.meaning: A deliberately shared and reviewed event records completion of a trusted protocol run.
signals.claim_boundary: Completion is not usefulness or efficacy. It is counted only from accepted opt-in events, never inferred from navigation or time on page.
signals.interpretation: Observed value counts only reviewed explicit opt-in events (protocol_completed). It is not a population total and does not imply later-stage outcomes.

signals.meaning: A deliberately shared and reviewed event contains explicit helpful or not-helpful feedback.
signals.claim_boundary: Helpfulness is self-reported and opt-in. A rate is unknown when there are no reviewed helpfulness events; it is not reported as 0%.
signals.interpretation: There are no reviewed helpfulness observations, so the count is zero but the helpfulness rate remains unknown (null), not 0%.

signals.meaning: A later real use is explicitly reported and can be distinguished from the original attempt without passive identity tracking.
signals.claim_boundary: Brali intentionally has no passive cross-session identity. Repeat use must remain unknown until a separate explicit, privacy-safe reporting contract exists; page views, cookies, local storage, and repeated anonymous events are not substitutes.
signals.interpretation: Brali does not currently collect this signal. Unknown remains null rather than being presented as zero.

signals.meaning: An external integration explicitly reports use of Brali through an agent or tool path.
signals.claim_boundary: This counts accepted integration reports, not MCP/API calls, active integrations, installed agents, or unique external users. Provider/runtime telemetry is separate unless explicitly reviewed and imported.
signals.interpretation: Observed value counts only reviewed explicit opt-in events (integration_reported). It is not a population total and does not imply later-stage outcomes.

signals.meaning: A later real-world result after using a Brali method is explicitly reported with enough context to distinguish it from protocol completion or immediate helpfulness.
signals.claim_boundary: Brali currently does not collect a dedicated downstream-outcome signal. Helpful feedback and protocol completion must not be presented as downstream efficacy or causal impact.
signals.interpretation: Brali does not currently collect this signal. Unknown remains null rather than being presented as zero.

rules: Unknown is represented as null, never silently converted to zero.
Reviewed event counts describe accepted opt-in observations only; they are not population totals.
Page discovery and traffic measurements stay separate from product outcome observations.
A later-stage signal must never be inferred from an earlier-stage signal: open is not attempt, attempt is not completion, completion is not usefulness, usefulness is not downstream outcome.
External provider metrics remain provider measurements unless an explicit reviewed import contract says otherwise.
interpretation: This report distinguishes measurable reviewed opt-in observations from signals Brali does not collect. Null means unknown/uncollected; numeric zero means zero accepted reviewed events of that explicit type, not zero real-world users, opens, attempts or outcomes.
